summary.text: Yassamin Ansari is the Democratic incumbent for Arizona's 3rd Congressional District, first elected in 2024 to succeed Ruben Gallego, who ran for U.S. Senate. A former United Nations climate policy advisor, she served on the Phoenix City Council, where she became vice mayor. In the House she serves on the Natural Resources and Oversight and Government Reform committees.

paragraphs.text: Ansari was born in Seattle, Washington. Her parents immigrated from Iran and moved to the Phoenix area in 1997, according to her Ballotpedia survey, and her office describes her as a daughter of immigrants.
She earned a bachelor's degree from Stanford University in 2014 and a master's degree from the University of Cambridge in 2015.

She began her career in international climate policy and says she was the youngest advisor on the UN Secretary-General's climate team under both Ban Ki-moon and Antonio Guterres, working on the Paris Agreement and later leading youth engagement for the 2019 UN Climate Action Summit.
Ansari won a March 9, 2021, runoff for the Phoenix City Council's District 7 seat. Her office says she was the youngest woman ever elected to the council, and she later served as vice mayor.

On the council she created what her campaign describes as the nation's first Office of Heat Response and Mitigation. She announced in March 2024 that she would resign on March 28 to focus on her congressional campaign.
Ansari won the 2024 general election for Arizona's 3rd District with 70.9 percent of the vote and took office on January 3, 2025.
Her office says she was the youngest woman in the 119th Congress and the first Iranian American Democrat in Congress, and that she serves as Freshman Class President for House Democrats.

She is ranking member of the Natural Resources Committee's Energy and Mineral Resources Subcommittee and also sits on the Oversight and Government Reform Committee. She advanced from the July 21, 2026 Democratic primary.
